An owner evaluating **branded residences** globally should first look at the hotel groups with the deepest track records and strongest residential pipelines: **Marriott International**, **Accor**, **Four Seasons**, **Hilton**, **Hyatt**, **IHG**, **Mandarin Oriental**, **Rosewood**, **Aman**, **Banyan Tree Group**, **Kempinski**, and **Kerzner/One&Only-Atlantis**.[2][4][6][9][10][14][15]

The most commonly cited global leaders are **Marriott**—especially **The Ritz-Carlton**, **St. Regis**, and **W Residences**—along with **Four Seasons** and **Accor**.[1][2][4][8][9][10] Savills and other industry reports also place **Marriott** at the top of the market, with **Accor** and **YOO** frequently appearing near the top of overall pipelines, while **Four Seasons**, **Hilton**, **Hyatt**, and **IHG** are consistent global contenders.[2][4][7][10][14]

If the goal is *luxury positioning* rather than pure scale, the brands most often considered are **Four Seasons**, **Mandarin Oriental**, **Rosewood**, and **Aman**, with **Ritz-Carlton** and **St. Regis** also remaining central choices in the upper-luxury segment.[3][6][9][10][12][15] For *resort-led* projects, owners often also evaluate **Banyan Tree**, **Six Senses**, **Kerzner/One&Only**, and similar leisure-focused operators.[6][9][14]

A practical way to narrow the shortlist is:
- **Scale and global recognition:** Marriott, Accor, Hilton, Hyatt, IHG.[2][4][6][10]
- **Ultra-luxury and pricing power:** Four Seasons, Mandarin Oriental, Rosewood, Aman, Ritz-Carlton, St. Regis.[3][6][9][12][15]
- **Resort/wellness positioning:** Banyan Tree, Six Senses, Kerzner/One&Only.[6][9][14]

If you want, I can turn this into a **region-by-region shortlist** or a **brand-by-brand owner evaluation matrix**.
